quest.title: Bonds of Melody
quest.description: Razor decides to make some Thousand-Wind Wine personally to better understand his human parents. However, which ingredients, specifically, was Venti's song referring to?
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x60, Festive Fever x50, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

chapter.num: Of Ballads and Brews: Act II
chapter.title: Bonds of Melody

talks.objective: Wait until the appointed time (08:00 – 10:00 two days later)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Where's the heck's Razor? Paimon thought he would've been here by now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, he had a pretty big day when we last saw him... Do you think he fell asleep when he got back and is still snoozing away now?

choices.text: Sounds more like something you'd do than Razor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fair enough, you're right. Let's keep waiting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, since we've got some time on our hands, let's put our heads together and try to figure out that poem! Tone-Deaf Bard mentioned some ingredients, but they all sounded super abstract:

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: An explorer's courage, a love tender and true, a defender's will, and... the thousand winds'... "song of good cheer"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you have any ideas?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeesh, that's even more abstract! How do we go about looking for this wine's "character"? Where do we start?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The Adventurers' Guild, the Church of Favonius...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Are you saying that it has something to do with Mondstadt's institutions?

choices.text: Yes... And as for the word "defender"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that... actually makes a surprising amount of sense. So the poem wasn't talking about any specific ingredients after all? More like... the general gist?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now that you mention it, it just so happens that all the institutions you mentioned are organizers of the Weinlesefest!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Wait, this is way too big of a coincidence! That Tone-Deaf Bard, did he just make this all up on the spot!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Perhaps he did... as a way of helping us to help Razor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In that case, the last part about the thousand winds' song of cheer must be code for the toasting ceremony! Ohoho, now we're cookin'! We'll crack your riddle-recipe yet, Tone-Deaf Bard!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When Razor gets here, let's visit all the places you mentioned and talk to some people we know there. We definitely should be able to find some more clues that way.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: #{F#Miss}{M#Mr.} Honorary Knight! Paimon!

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I'm sorry! I'm late...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's alright, we were just chatting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}'s pretty smart, so thanks to {M#him}{F#her}, we're finally onto something!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hello, Klee, and Razor.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Hi. I was on my way, then I saw Klee.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: They let me out for Weinlesefest!

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Albedo is super busy helping Timaeus fix his recipe for an Extra-Strong Sobriety Potion, so he doesn't have time to come play with me right now. I'm just playing by myself instead.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: But it's so cool! All the grown-ups in Mondstadt are out to celebrate the festival. Everyone's smiling and having loads of fun!

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: I wanted to join in too. So I made a whole bunch of stuff so I can celebrate with everyone in my very own way!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Very own way"... Uh oh, this does not bode well coming from Klee.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: And that's when I bumped into Razor.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Razor was acting kinda different than usual, like he was thinking about something. So I asked him, "What happened?"

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: And then Razor said that he was looking for his mommy!

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I did not say mommy.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: It's okay, silly! Mommies are important people, so finding your mommy is a super important job. That's why Klee's gonna come help!

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: *panting* Razor... Razor... finally, I found you.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Bennett?

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Oh, haha, look who's here! Hey, everyone.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Here, this is for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... a Small Lamp Grass?

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Yup, that's right. I tripped up on it this morning and took a little tumble.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: I did a full faceplant, but somehow, this little thing came out completely unscathed. That's when I knew it was destined to go into your wine mix!

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Bennett, how did you manage to trip up on a Small Lamp Grass?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that's true. They do glow, after all...

choices.text: To be fair, they only glow at night...

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: No, no, I wasn't talking about the glowing. What I meant was, they're really big and easy to spot. So I don't get how you didn't see it.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Haha, ah, I was just running too fast and got careless, I guess.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: (Okay, I guess maybe I won't tell them about the other faceplants that came after that...)

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Anyway, I've been all over the place trying to find Razor this morning. Everyone I asked told me I'd just missed him.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Good thing I've caught up now, I can finally catch my breath...

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: #Thanks, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: How did you know... I need ingredients?

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Oh, that? Yeah, interesting story.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: This lady came to see Master Cyrus, asking for the Adventurers' Guild's support with the Weinlesefest. Said she was the librarian. Anyway, she mentioned your situation too, and asked if we could help...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, Lisa is doing some real work for once?

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Ohhh! So that was Lisa? People say she's crazy intelligent but just doesn't go out much... First time I've ever seen her.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: I thought long and hard about what ingredients to pick, and came up with a load of suggestions that I was gonna discuss with you...

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: But then I realized that Small Lamp Grass was clearly the best. It shines a light to guide the way for explorers in the dark. Doesn't that sound like a wonderful thing?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: ...Apologies... for the trouble.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Ahh, don't gimme that! I get how you must be feeling about all of this. Besides, you gotta help out your friends, right?

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: If my family... uh, well, my dads ever needed help one day, I know you'd be there for me too.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Can I help, too? Please, take me with you, pleeease! I wanna join in!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Klee's in high spirits today. She seems more excited by this festival than anyone.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Bennett, before now... you never talk about your family.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Ahh, haha, well that's because I never met my parents. I was raised by some of the older adventurers in the guild. So we're not exactly a typical family.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: But if you do want to hear about them, I can tell you some of my dads' stories. Hmm... okay, I'll start with the most awesome one.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Aw, Bennett...

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: You can be Mommy's kid, just like Klee! My mom is super nice — she'll take great care of you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!?

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: I really appreciate the thought, Klee. But I'm afraid I can't accept your offer...

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: I already have my dads and all my friends... And let's not forget that I'm the leader of Benny's Adventure Team. You don't need to worry about me.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Oh, okay. I got it. Um, then have this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A Jumpy Dumpty?

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Yeah! It's a lazy, dopey Jumpy Dumpty that always dozes and never explodes! I hope you guys can be best friends.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: ...Are you sure?

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Yep! Jumpy Dumpty will be happy to make a new friend, too.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I... also happy for you.

choices.text: I still have to look for ingredients with Razor...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good idea. Maybe Klee will bring Bennett some good luck, and the adventure will go smoothly. And you might just find some treasures you've never noticed before!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course... It's also highly possible that Klee will be the only one who gets lucky...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, on the flip side, Klee won't be getting into any trouble with Bennett there. And this way, she'll still get to enjoy the Weinlesefest!

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Cool, don't worry about a thing! We'll look after each other.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Yay! Adventure! Treasure! Weinlesefest! Let's go, let's go!

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Oh... wait, but what about Wolfie? Wolfie— uh, I mean Razor needs looking after. Honorary Knight, Paimon, you'd better take care of Razor, okay? Make sure he finds his mommy.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Mm...

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: ...Good luck.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: See ya later, folks.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, it's so nice to see everyone in such a good mood.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh...! Paimon almost forgot the whole reason we came here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Razor, {NICKNAME} and Paimon were just chatting about the ingredients Venti mentioned in his poem. We think that they're actually a description of the wine's characteristics.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Plus, it seems like each of them means something special to one of the three big institutions in Mondstadt. So, if we talk to some people we know at each place, maybe we'll find what you're looking for.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's wrong? Something on your mind? Do you want to talk about it?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Yes. These days, I think a lot.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: #I am not... smart. Not like teacher, not like {NICKNAME}. But... I still have to think.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Everyone is ready to help, but... some things, I must do myself.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I don't understand human father and mother... but I must find a way to understand.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Maybe I can learn about other people's father and mother first, then think about my own father and mother.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: That's why I want to ask questions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's great! Keep at it, and you'll definitely find the answer eventually.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Never knew Bennett is... like me.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: When he talks about "dads," his scent changes.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Warm, like a bed of straw in the sun.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's find more people to speak to.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! We should head back into the city. Let's find a friendly face at the Church of Favonius!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, now who does Razor know best at the church...

response.speaker: Marcel
response.text: Excuse me, I couldn't help but overhear that you're about to head back into the city. Is that right?

response.speaker: Marcel
response.text: I'm waiting on a fruit cart from the city. It should be here now, but... I'm getting worried that something may have happened on the way, but I can't leave the festival to check up on it...

response.speaker: Marcel
response.text: Would you be able to do me a huge favor, and keep an eye out for the cart on your way back?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ummm... Well, if it's on the way...

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Okay, we go. I go too.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Everyone helps me. Now I have chance, to help everyone.

response.speaker: Marcel
response.text: That's wonderful, thank you so much!

choices.text: Why don't you two go adventuring together?
Definitely time to take a break...
It doesn't help during the day.
It makes me think of the Knights of Favonius.

talks.objective: Search for the late cart in the wild

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: *sniff*... This way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Paimon sees the cart, but what are these hilichurls doing here!? Do they want some fresh fruit now, too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, to the rescue!

talks.objective: Scare off the hilichurls and save the cart

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, finally. These hilichurls are a little too obsessed with food for their own good... But never mind that, are you okay? Did they hurt you?

dialogues.speaker: Rolf
dialogues.text: Phew... I'm fine, thanks to you. You were just in time. Any later, and all you'd have found here is a pile of pulp... and I don't think there'd be much left of the fruit, either.

choices.text: They're still waiting for you at the festival.

response.speaker: Rolf
response.text: Got it. Well, thanks again! I'd better not delay this delivery any longer, so goodbye and Happy Weinlesefest!

response.speaker: Rolf
response.text: Thanks to you, too, kiddo.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Mm.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Enemy following.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: "Enemy"? Heh, I think we're a little closer than that.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: On some level, you could even say that we're brother and sister.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Rosaria! What the heck are you doing here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait... Actually, turning up at random places is pretty normal for you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, next question: What the heck do you mean "brother and sister"?

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Varka taught you how to use that sword, I take it? Swift but powerful. Heh, I can spot that old-timer's style anywhere.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: I see you're not much of a talker. Well, there's something else you could learn from Varka. Never lost for words, even when he has nothing to say... It'd be good conversation practice for you. Just a shame we have no idea when he'll be back.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: It's okay. I will wait.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Brother and sister...? Varka...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Paimon gets it. Varka is a father figure to both of them, so that makes them family — just not by blood.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Well, blood relations are overrated anyway, don't you think?

choices.text: I think the bond of blood is a strong one.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: #Ah, I almost forgot. You have a {M#sister}{F#brother}.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Cold, dark grown-up... You also don't remember what your real mother and real father look like?

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Huh... So you're helping him dig up some info on his biological parents? And trying to help him build a concept of family along the way?

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Alright, you got me.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: I barely have any memories of my birth parents... The last time I saw them was long before I had any understanding of the world around me.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: But that seems pretty common. Even in this day and age, there are plenty of people in the world who can't stop thinking about their families, but will never get to see them.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Anyway, if you're never gonna meet someone, it's not worth spending mental energy on them. It's more important to focus on the kind of person you want to become.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: No! You are wrong about this.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Lupical protect each other. Human family also important. Must care about them.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: ...Fine. So let's say you do find out who your parents were, and they were saints. Or the opposite, they were complete monsters. What then?

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: How would that affect your life choices? What would you do about it?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Ummm...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whew, Rosaria's take is a little on the nose... That's a hard one for Razor to answer.

choices.text: But it's normal to be curious.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Don't get me wrong, I'm not trying to make this any more difficult than it already is. But Razor's feeling lost and confused right now, and all the other Mondstadters we know are too sunny and bright to tell it like it really is...

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: ...The sun nurtures many good things, but it can't do anything about the problems lurking in the shadows.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Rosaria...

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Alright, I'll leave it there. Take this flower, it's icy cold — just like me.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Barbara's busy preparing the sung poetry event for the Weinlesefest. She couldn't get away, so I picked an ingredient out on behalf of the church.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But can we really use a Mist Flower? Won't it freeze the entire barrel?

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: No, not now that I've dealt with it. The bard did say to think "freedom," didn't he? So go on, take it. It won't be a problem.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, Rosaria, you're more thoughtful than Paimon realized...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Uh, wait, you heard the bard say that? Were you spying on us!?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Thank you...

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Don't mention it. It's nothing. Varka's been a big help to me in the past, so just consider it returning a favor. Besides... if I'm your older sister, I might as well act like it.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Good luck finding your answers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now you see her, now you don't... Paimon's slowly getting used to her style.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh well, as "love tender and true" goes, that was pretty awkward, but... still counts, right? Now all that's left is the Knights of Favonius.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Razor, are you still thinking about what Rosaria said?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Her words, are like Mist Flower. They are cold, and they sting.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: But cold also good for wounds. Like Wolfhook.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I need to, think about it. Maybe then, I will understand.

choices.text: It'll take some time, there's no need to rush it.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Okay.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I will come with you. I think while we walk.

choices.text: The urge to know is understandable.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: I get it. In the final moments of your life, the people there with you won't necessarily be your blood relatives.

choices.text: Keep your eyes peeled on the road.

talks.objective: Go to the Knights of Favonius Headquarters

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: ...So you see, you're the best person for this.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Oho, just in time. Lisa and I were just talking about Razor's situation.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Where were we... Ah, yes, the barrel!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? But obviously, the knights part is supposed to be "a defender's will." But what kind of ingredient is a barrel?

choices.text: Obviously that's not what he meant.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... F—Fair enough...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Hehe... Oh, Paimon, don't worry, you'll get your ingredient. I've already tasked someone with sorting it out.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: The person is very conscientious, and wants to properly research their contribution. So it may take some time, but hopefully it'll be worth the wait.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: As for the barrel... how else were you planning on mixing all the ingredients? Surely not in the giant cooking pot at Dadaupa Gorge?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: After much deliberation, I realized this was a job for the most sociable and savviest member in our ranks, the Cavalry Captain. So I asked him to take a trip to the Dawn Winery, and somehow bring back a wine barrel.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: *sigh* Alright, spare me the flattery, Lisa. We're all friends here, and I know you're only trying to help your student.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: ...But I haven't been back there in a long time. This could be quite difficult to accomplish in just a single trip.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Difficult? For you? Don't be silly, negotiating is your biggest strength.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Weinlesefest is one of the most important festivals in Mondstadt, and you know how Diluc thinks better than anyone.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Just drop a few little hints, like how this is the first festival Mondstadt has had in a long time, we're short on much-needed supplies for a multitude of reasons... Oh, who can help us?

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: When he hears that, I guarantee you he'll offer to help out with finances and sourcing goods.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lisa's literally trying to extort Master Diluc!

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Hmm... I suppose. Alright, I'll head out right away.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, he didn't take much persuading!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, and Paimon was just about to thank Lisa for the things she's been doing for Razor behind the scenes...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't even know whose side to be on anymore...

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: #{NICKNAME} and teacher, did a lot for me. A lot of work.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: But me... I still can't answer questions. So useless.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Dear me, what's gotten you so upset, my little wolf cub? We can't have you being so down in the dumps.

choices.text: Some questions, he can't stop thinking about.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Ah, I see.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Hmm. Cutie, how about you keep Kaeya company while I stay here and help Razor process his feelings? As his teacher, I owe him some tutelage anyway.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Come and collect him in a few days' time. The last ingredient should be ready by then as well.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Splendid. I was just thinking about how nice it would be to have some company on my trip.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I don't know what is right, but I trust Teacher. I accept.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Run along now, and don't forget to tell Diluc that the Knights of Favonius send our regards.

choices.text: Lisa, you're a godsend. Thank you.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Well, aren't you a sweet one? But this is as much my business as yours. It's my pleasure, really.

choices.text: That would be a "Suspicious Thousand-Wind Wine"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is your brain half-asleep or something? It doesn't make any sense at all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi there, Master Diluc!

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Oh? I was just wondering who'd be coming all the way out here during the Weinlesefest. So it's you two.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: ...And you, too.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Brrr, so cold. Almost enough to make me feel unwelcome here, Master Diluc.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Don't forget that this is my home, too. I'm fairly certain that taking a trip home during festival season is a universal custom, common to all the cultures of Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Please get to the point.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: The point is one that you've already raised yourself: the Weinlesefest.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: To celebrate this long-awaited festival, the Acting Grand Master has been coordinating with both the church and the Adventurers' Guild to host a series of events.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, given the financial situation of the Knights of Favonius... Well, I'm sure you can imagine...

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: And the Knights of Favonius's woes have what, exactly, to do with me?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Hey, no need to be so cruel. Even I'm not going to take that. Everyone's just doing the best they can for Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Now, I can't remember the last time I tasted Dawn Winery's Weinlesefest special... And I'm sure the Mondstadt populace would echo this sentiment.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Are you going to deny others the opportunity to drink to their hearts' content just because you don't like to drink yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Check it out, Kaeya's not-so-subtly asking for freebies... He's actually doing it...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What a guy.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Anyway, speaking of the knights, everyone dearly hopes that you'll rejoin our ranks again one day. Then we'll be one big, happy family again.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: If we were able to enjoy the sterling reputation of Master Diluc, my... I'm sure people would be queuing for our charity booth all the way to Falcon Coast...

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: ...Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Give that silver tongue of yours a rest. You might need it to maintain public order at the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Duly noted on the financial issues you raised. I'll have Elzer follow up with Hertha in more detail.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: And I just so happen to have a batch of wine that I can offer as a token of appreciation to everyone that has been working so hard for the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Shall I address it to you personally?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: That would be an absurd request, even for me. The words "with compliments from the Dawn Winery" ought never be preceded by "To the Cavalry Captain." Is that not the unwritten rule?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: You're better informed than I thought. In that case, I will leave this with Adelinde and keep everything anonymous.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: I really can't thank you enough.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Master Diluc is so generous! That's all Paimon needs to get that warm, fuzzy feeling... which is just as well, since she won't be allowed to drink a drop.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Are you two here regarding the Weinlesefest, too?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Diluc that you're helping Razor to make Thousand-Wind Wine...

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Poor Razor. He grew up so fast, and he's still looking for his father. Master Diluc, we really ought to lend him a hand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How come Klee said he's looking for his mom, but Kaeya says he's looking for his dad...? It might make more sense to them, but it's gonna get confusing for everyone else!

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: It's okay. I understand.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: We have a spare barrel in the winery. It's a little old, but it's been specially treated for durability. You could leave it next to a Flaming Flower all day and there wouldn't be a scratch. I think that one should satisfy your needs.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds great, we'll take it! When can we come fetch it?

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: No need. I'll have someone deliver it to the festival market. Just collect it from the Angel's Share stand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, you always make things so nice and easy for us, Master Diluc! Hehe, thanks a lot. Razor will really appreciate it.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: You're more than welcome. Helping each other is what friends do.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Wonderful. Always eager to help, and never forgets to return a favor. That's the Master Diluc I know.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: ...It's nearly dinner time. Would you care to stay for a meal?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: How time flies... I'll be on my way, then...

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Hmph.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: How did you put it? Ah, yes: "Taking a trip home during festival season is a universal custom, common to all the cultures of Teyvat." Now that even Master Diluc has made an offer... Are you quite sure you won't stay for a meal after coming all this way, Master Kaeya?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: I couldn't possibly, Adelinde. I wouldn't want to trouble you.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: Oh, don't say that. How often do I get a chance to indulge my dear Master Kaeya, hmm? Tea for the Cavalry Captain when you visit in an official capacity doesn't count. I only get to spoil you if you'll let me cook for you.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Oh, uh...

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: What happened to your swagger? Lost for words?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: ...Ahaha... Diluc, you—

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Surely you wouldn't dream of disappointing Adelinde?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The more the merrier.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: ...Alright then. I'll take you up on the offer. Adelinde, one more set of cutlery, please, if you'd be so kind.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The group dines to the sound of Kaeya's jesting and Diluc's disapproving grunts...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oof, Paimon's so full... Adelinde's cooking is amazing. Everything looked and tasted so beautiful.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Glad you liked it. You're welcome to join again anytime.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: #Oh? Then I may have to tag along on {NICKNAME}'s adventures more often in the future.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, Kaeya's back to his usual ways.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Alright, now that our task is complete and our bellies are full, it's time for me to get back to work.

response.speaker: Adelinde
response.text: Take care, Master Kaeya. Have a safe trip back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We should get going as well. Lisa's taking care of Razor, but the Weinlesefest can't do without us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See you next time, Master Diluc!

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Indeed. Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: We're going through a ton of fruit this Weinlesefest... I really need that cart to get here safely.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: My heart, feels like, rotten berries. So sour.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: I don't understand what I should do...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Aw, alright. I'll teach you a very special magic trick that can make all your troubles disappear in the blink of an eye.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: But before we do that, let's warm up with something a little bit easier, hmm? Let's practice some talking.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: That way, the next time somebody helps you, or you have a different opinion from the rest of the group, you'll be able to express what you think clearly and precisely.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Okay!

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: I will do my best.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Family, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Don't mind me. You should probably head back and get some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: I'm not the most familiar with Razor, but you can contact me if you ever need help.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: It's been a long time since I last saw Masters Diluc and Kaeya sharing a meal together. The atmosphere was... ahem, was not something that a maid of my lowly stature should be commenting on.

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, thank you so much for visiting. I hope to see you again soon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kaeya, you're fond of a good drink, aren't you? Weinlesefest must be right up your alley.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, Kaeya...?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Oh, I'm sorry, my mind was elsewhere... What was your question?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph, never mind. Nothing that important.
